ui.supportsXlsxAndCsvTheFirstReadable: Supports .xlsx, .xls, and .csv. The first readable worksheet in each file is selected by default; select more if needed. Expand a file to preview its source data and adjust its header row. For legacy Chinese CSV files, try GB18030.

ui.upTo30FilesAnd100000: Up to 30 files and 100,000 data rows per batch; 50 MB per file. Joins, aggregation, and complex merged-cell layouts are not supported. Formulas use saved results only; recalculate and save in Excel before importing.
ui.storeOrderIdsAndSkusAsText: Store order IDs and SKUs as text in source files. Existing leading zeros and simple zero-padding formats are preserved; digits already lost in the source cannot be recovered. Amounts are not calculated, converted between currencies, or rescaled automatically.
ui.temporaryDataIsClearedOnExitOr: Temporary data is cleared on exit or the next startup. The rule library stays in the local application data directory. Save downloaded results where you need them.

guide.title: Merge spreadsheets in 5 steps
guide.intro: Different column names are fine. Choose your output columns, match each source, and download one table.
guide.templateMeaning: Which columns you want in the final file.
guide.ruleMeaning: Where each output column gets its data.
guide.import.title: Import your files
guide.import.body: Drag in your files or click Choose files. Select the worksheets to merge, then click Next: confirm template.
guide.import.tip: This example uses two grade tables with different headers: 12 records each, 24 records in total.
guide.import.alt: Two student-grade files imported, with 24 rows and two worksheets selected.
guide.import.caption: 1. Import both files and check the selected worksheets.
guide.template.title: Select and confirm a template
guide.template.body: Choose a saved template and review its columns. Each new batch starts without a selection. Dismiss the missing-template prompt to choose, or go to Output template to create one.
guide.template.tip: For this example, select Student grades with Student ID, Name, Subject, and numeric Score. Click Confirm template, next.
guide.template.alt: Confirm template step showing a saved Student grades template and its four output columns.
guide.template.caption: 2. Select a saved template for this batch and confirm the output columns.
guide.mapping.title: Match each source column
guide.mapping.body: Click Configure & confirm for each source. Choose the source column for every output column, then click Confirm mapping.
guide.mapping.tip: For Student ID, choose {id} in the first file and Student ID in the second. For Score, choose {score} or Points.
guide.mapping.alt: Field-mapping dialog matching {id} to Student ID, {name} to Name, {subject} to Subject, and {score} to Score.
guide.mapping.caption: 3. Different source headers can feed the same output column.
guide.result.title: Merge and download
guide.result.body: Click Start merge, wait for completion, then Download merged Excel. The example produces 24 valid records in one worksheet.
guide.result.tip: The Excel file contains one sheet of valid records. Check problem rows on the results page. Exact duplicates are retained and flagged.
guide.result.alt: Completed merge of two student-grade files: 24 valid rows, zero problem rows, and a download button.
guide.result.caption: 5. Download one workbook with 24 valid records.
guide.reuse.title: Create, edit, and reuse templates
guide.reuse.body: Open Output template to manage the template library. Create or edit columns, then Save file & add to library to choose a folder. Save as new template keeps the original library entry. Each batch needs an explicit template selection; saved source rules can still be reused after review.
guide.headers.question: The header is not on row 1, or Chinese text looks wrong?
guide.headers.answer: Expand the imported file and set Header row to the row containing the column names. For a Chinese CSV with garbled text, try GB18030 under Character encoding.
guide.backup.question: Can I back up my setup?
guide.backup.answer: Save each output template as JSON in a folder you choose, and import it to restore it. Source rules → Export rule library backs up the full setup, including the template library. Importing that backup replaces the current setup.
guide.files.question: What stays saved when I close the tool?
guide.files.answer: Original files stay unchanged. Templates and saved rules stay on this computer. Closing the browser does not stop the service; stopping the service clears imported batches and temporary results. Download your result before stopping.
guide.limits: Import: .xlsx / .xls / .csv · Up to 30 files, 100,000 data rows per batch, 50 MB per file · Export: .xlsx. Screenshots use fictional student records; the same steps work for sales and other tables.

guide.preview.title: Preview the converted records
guide.preview.body: Click Preview converted data. Check the first 20 records: make sure IDs, names, subjects, and scores are in the right columns.
guide.preview.tip: If anything is wrong, return to the source rules. Change the template through step 2; changing it requires the mappings to be confirmed again.
guide.preview.alt: Preview step showing correctly mapped student IDs, names, subjects, scores, and passed checks.
guide.preview.caption: 4. Check a sample before processing all selected records.
